correctness.rationale: With gamma_i>0, g>0, g²<gamma_1 gamma_2 and nonnegative nonzero incentives, scaling v_i=sqrt(gamma_i)x_i yields t∈(0,1). The two private best responses are v2=y2, v1=y1+t v2 and give a unique nonnegative Nash. The planner Hessian [[1,-t],[-t,1]] has eigenvalues 1±t>0, and its positive inverse maps nonnegative nonzero y to a feasible unique optimum. The exact payoff identity at Nash and quadratic inverse formula give W_NE=D/2>0 and W_opt=(y1²+2ty1y2+y2²)/(2(1-t²)); the lower and upper bound residuals factor as strictly nonnegative rational functions with exact zero sets y1=0 and y2=0. Continuity covers the complete interval; nilpotency M²=0 is immediate. At t≥1, the diagonal ray makes welfare unbounded; n=1 is efficient. Exact rational replay tests 945 heterogeneous-cost configurations plus endpoints and high-t checks; all passed. None of the proof rests on finite enumeration.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The new formula cannot follow by specializing the symmetric spectral theorem: its response matrix is strictly triangular and nonsymmetric, while every eigenvalue remains zero. Nor is it a mere restatement of the potential-maximizer bound in Rokade et al., as the latter evaluates a different action for asymmetric games. The directed opinion-formation model has a different payoff. The exact interval and uniform divergence even at zero response spectral radius remain unaddressed by the materials inspected. Existing general quadratic optimization identities are ingredients rather than demonstrated statements of this welfare classification.

originality.rationale: The motivating work proves a symmetric homogeneous-cost spectral PoA result and explicitly asks for asymmetric, heterogeneous-cost counterparts. The closest inspected published 2026 LQ welfare bounds likewise assume symmetric undirected adjacency; the relevant 2025 asymmetric α-potential welfare bound uses a different approximate-equilibrium optimizer and imposes distinct restrictions. The claimed exact true-Nash interval, its sharp direct-incentive equality cases, and universal zero-spectral-radius blowup were not implied by the inspected passages. This is best-knowledge originality rather than a priority guarantee; general LQ welfare coverage remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: Unlocated classical or modern sharp welfare bounds for asymmetric two-agent quadratic network games may subsume the closed interval.
The 2016 directed opinion formation paper was compared at abstract level only; its distinct utility model makes implication unlikely but not verified against all text.
Elementary 2×2 matrix algebra is standard; the novelty claim attaches to the motivated full incentive-uniform sharp PoA classification, not to inverse-matrix manipulation.
No independent literature audit has been conducted.

value.rationale: The source explicitly poses the welfare theory challenge under asymmetric spillovers and heterogeneous effort costs. This theorem answers a sharp natural first case, rather than selecting an arbitrary isolated incentive vector: it classifies the entire attainable interval across all nonnegative nonzero incentives at fixed economics, pins down both endpoints and equality cases, and shows even the BEST attainable ratio diverges while strategic-response spectral radius is identically zero. Consequently a spectrum-only welfare estimate cannot be transferred from symmetric to directed networks. It also identifies the sharp planner-feasibility boundary and minimal number of agents. It makes no unsupported inference to general networks.
